# gh-1746: [GOAL] Session disk hygiene: opt-in retention cap + age-aware sweep (nothing auto-deleted unless configured)

## Description

## Goal — Session disk hygiene (v2 — revised framing)

One sentence: **the sessions root gets an opt-in retention policy (`sessions.retention`) — a total-size cap enforced by an age-aware, live/named-safe sweep at boot — so a workspace of marathon sessions can never quietly eat the disk, while with no config nothing is EVER auto-deleted.**

Today nothing bounds the sessions root: a single marathon workspace holds 425 MB + 4.8 GB transcripts (measured, dmtools slug), macOS has already throttled fa for 8.6 GB of dirty writes in 15 h (YuryBY's #1745 diag log). The only tools are manual: `fa session repair` shrinks a ledger, `delete` removes one session, `cleanupEmptySessions` removes EMPTY files. There is no cap, no sweep, no usage visibility beyond `/sessions` listing.

## Why this framing

- **v1 of this issue ("configurable full-open bound") is RETRACTED as the framing** — it answered a memory-risk question (how big a file may be fully opened), not the owner's actual ask (stop sessions filling the disk). The full-open knob stays a legitimate second-tier follow-up, listed under Non-goals.
- "Auto-clean by default" is rejected as the default posture: silently deleting session history is the one irreversible action fa must never take unconfigured. Opt-in cap (variant B below) is the recommendation; the alternative (default cap) is an explicit open question for the owner.

## Architecture

Named components:

- **Config** (user file, tolerant section — unknown keys note, never boot-fail):
  ```yaml
  sessions:
    retention:
      maxTotalBytes: 0      # 0/absent = NO cap, nothing is ever auto-deleted (default)
      minAgeDays: 14        # a session younger than this is never swept
      keepNamed: true       # named sessions (--session <name>) are always exempt
      sweep: boot           # boot | off — when the sweep runs (off = cap set but manual-only)
  ```
- **Usage walk** — O(directory entries), never O(file bytes): stat-based size + last-used (mtime; a live presence marker overrides recency), reusing the header-only listing the picker already streams.
- **Sweep** (`SessionRetentionSweeper`, pure-Dart core over `ExecutionEnv`): when total > `maxTotalBytes`, delete oldest-last-used first until under the cap, skipping: live sessions (presence file), named sessions (`keepNamed`), anything younger than `minAgeDays`, and the CURRENT session. Every deletion logs one line (file, size, age, reason). If the exempt set alone exceeds the cap, STOP and emit a loud note naming the blockers — never force.
- **Session-owned artifacts die with the session**: the transcript JSONL plus its sidecars in the same sweep unit — `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml`, `spills/<sessionId>/`, trajectory blobs `<sid>/`. Presence files are garbage-collected separately (they are not user data; #1660/#1740 already touched them).
- **Visibility**: `/sessions` gains a usage footer (`total X GB across N sessions, cap Y`); `fa sessions clean [--dry-run]` runs the sweep manually with a full report (what would be / was deleted, freed bytes, exemptions).
- Degradation: absent section = byte-identical today; a cap set but unreachable exemptions = note, no deletion loop.

## Capability surface

| Surface | Today | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Total disk cap | none | `maxTotalBytes`, opt-in |
| Auto-delete | none (manual delete only) | boot sweep, oldest-first, exempt live/named/young |
| Manual verb | `fa session repair`, per-file delete | `fa sessions clean --dry-run` + apply |
| Usage visibility | `/sessions` list only | total + per-slug + cap footer |
| Sidecar cleanup | none | dies with its session |

Tiering: **core** = config + sweeper + `fa sessions clean` + `/sessions` footer; **second tier** = app Settings surface, Trash-style archive instead of delete (`retention.archive: true` moves to `.fah/trash/`); **excluded** — spills/bash-jobs GLOBAL caps (their own growth has separate cards; only session-scoped subdirs ride this sweep), and any compaction of LIVE sessions (repair owns that).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — no `sessions:` section → no sweep ever runs, no boot note (byte-identical legacy; UT on config).
- **AC2** — cap set, total under → no deletions (UT).
- **AC3** — cap set, total over → oldest-last-used deleted until under; deleted set excludes live (presence), named (`keepNamed: true`), younger than `minAgeDays`, and the current session (IT with fake fs + fake clock).
- **AC4** — exempt-only overflow: nothing deleted, loud note names each blocker with size (UT).
- **AC5** — deleting a session removes its sidecars (`.tools/`, `spills/<sid>/`, trajectory blobs) in the same unit (IT).
- **AC6** — `fa sessions clean --dry-run` prints the exact plan (paths, sizes, ages, reasons) and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly the plan (E2E).
- **AC7** — every auto-deletion emits one log line; a sweep report persists to the boot log (IT asserts the lines).

## Test plan

- `UT-1..2` — config parse (absent/invalid/zero/valid) → AC1/2.
- `UT-3` — sweeper selection order + exemptions on a synthetic tree (AC3/4).
- `IT-1` — fake `ExecutionEnv` + fake clock: full sweep lifecycle incl. sidecars (AC3/5), log lines (AC7).
- `IT-2` — named/live/young exemption matrix (AC3).
- `E2E-1` — real fs temp root: `fa sessions clean --dry-run` then apply; `/sessions` footer numbers (AC6).
- `REG-1` **merge-blocking**: legacy-config fixture (no section) — no sweep, no notes, `/sessions` output byte-identical modulo the new footer line being ABSENT without a cap. **A red REG-1 job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**
- `REG-2` — presence/named sessions survive every sweep shape (property test over generated trees).

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — cap smaller than one marathon session: that session is still a deletion candidate (oldest-first) unless exempt — minAgeDays is the guard, not size.
- **E2** — race: a session becomes live mid-sweep → presence check immediately before each unlink; skip on mismatch.
- **E3** — clock skew / mtime touch by backup tools → last-used falls back to header `updatedAt` when mtime < header time.
- **E4** — symlinked session root: never follow links out of the root (path-escape test).
- **E5** — `sweep: off` with cap set: manual verb still works, boot never sweeps (only the over-cap note).
- **E6** — cross-slug fairness: cap is global across all project slugs; no slug starvation (oldest wins globally).

## Non-goals

- No default cap / no surprise deletion ever (that is the framing, restated as a guarantee).
- No live-session compaction/repair inside the sweep (`fa session repair` owns shrinking).
- No spills/bash-jobs global quotas — session-scoped subdirs only.
- The retracted v1 full-open knob (`sessions.maxFullOpenBytes`) — separate follow-up if wanted.
- No cloud/archive backend.

## Open questions

1. Default posture: **B (recommended)** — no cap unless set, boot NOTE (no action) when total crosses a soft warn threshold (e.g. 5 GiB) suggesting the keys; or **A** — ship a generous default cap (e.g. 20 GiB) with the same exemptions, so hygiene exists out of the box. Owner decides.
2. Delete vs archive-to-`.fah/trash/` for auto-swept sessions (manual verb always hard-deletes): recommend archive as second tier, delete for core.

## References

- Measured: dmtools slug 425 MB live + 4.8 GB kimi transcript; macOS throttle diag in #1745.
- Code: `session_repo.dart:413` (`cleanupEmptySessions` — empties only), `session_commands.dart` (manual delete), no retention anywhere (`grep retention|prune` — nothing).
- Related: #1745 (ledger growth — the producer side; this card is the consumer side), gh-1073/#1247 (per-record caps), #1590/#1594 (snapshot ledgers), #919 (bash_jobs log growth — adjacent, excluded here).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

    "description": "## Goal — Session disk hygiene (v2 — revised framing)

One sentence: **the sessions root gets an opt-in retention policy (`sessions.retention`) — a total-size cap enforced by an age-aware, live/named-safe sweep at boot — so a workspace of marathon sessions can never quietly eat the disk, while with no config nothing is EVER auto-deleted.**

Today nothing bounds the sessions root: a single marathon workspace holds 425 MB + 4.8 GB transcripts (measured, dmtools slug), macOS has already throttled fa for 8.6 GB of dirty writes in 15 h (YuryBY's #1745 diag log). The only tools are manual: `fa session repair` shrinks a ledger, `delete` removes one session, `cleanupEmptySessions` removes EMPTY files. - **v1 of this issue ("configurable full-open bound") is RETRACTED as the framing** — it answered a memory-risk question (how big a file may be fully opened), not the owner's actual ask (stop sessions filling the disk). ## Architecture

Named components:

- **Config** (user file, tolerant section — unknown keys note, never boot-fail):
  ```yaml
  sessions:
    retention:
      maxTotalBytes: 0      # 0/absent = NO cap, nothing is ever auto-deleted (default)
      minAgeDays: 14        # a session younger than this is never swept
      keepNamed: true       # named sessions (--session <name>) are always exempt
      sweep: boot           # boot | off — when the sweep runs (off = cap set but manual-only)
  ```
- **Usage walk** — O(directory entries), never O(file bytes): stat-based size + last-used (mtime; a live presence marker overrides recency), reusing the header-only listing the picker already streams.
- **Sweep** (`SessionRetentionSweeper`, pure-Dart core over `ExecutionEnv`): when total > `maxTotalBytes`, delete oldest-last-used first until under the cap, skipping: live sessions (presence file), named sessions (`keepNamed`), anything younger than `minAgeDays`, and the CURRENT session. Every deletion logs one line (file, size, age, reason). If the exempt set alone exceeds the cap, STOP and emit a loud note naming the blockers — never force.
- **Session-owned artifacts die with the session**: the transcript JSONL plus its sidecars in the same sweep unit — `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml`, `spills/<sessionId>/`, trajectory blobs `<sid>/`. Presence files are garbage-collected separately (they are not user data; #1660/#1740 already touched them).
- **Visibility**: `/sessions` gains a usage footer (`total X GB across N sessions, cap Y`); `fa sessions clean [--dry-run]` runs the sweep manually with a full report (what would be / was deleted, freed bytes, exemptions).
- Degradation: absent section = byte-identical today; a cap set but unreachable exemptions = note, no deletion loop.

| Surface | Today | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Total disk cap | none | `maxTotalBytes`, opt-in |
| Auto-delete | none (manual delete only) | boot sweep, oldest-first, exempt live/named/young |
| Manual verb | `fa session repair`, per-file delete | `fa sessions clean --dry-run` + apply |
| Usage visibility | `/sessions` list only | total + per-slug + cap footer |
| Sidecar cleanup | none | dies with its session |

- **AC6** — `fa sessions clean --dry-run` prints the exact plan (paths, sizes, ages, reasons) and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly the plan (E2E).
- **AC7** — every auto-deletion emits one log line; a sweep report persists to the boot log (IT asserts the lines).

## Test plan

- `UT-1..2` — config parse (absent/invalid/zero/valid) → AC1/2.
- `UT-3` — sweeper selection order + exemptions on a synthetic tree (AC3/4).
- `IT-1` — fake `ExecutionEnv` + fake clock: full sweep lifecycle incl. sidecars (AC3/5), log lines (AC7).
- `IT-2` — named/live/young exemption matrix (AC3).
- `E2E-1` — real fs temp root: `fa sessions clean --dry-run` then apply; `/sessions` footer numbers (AC6).
- `REG-1` **merge-blocking**: legacy-config fixture (no section) — no sweep, no notes, `/sessions` output byte-identical modulo the new footer line being ABSENT without a cap. **A red REG-1 job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**
- `REG-2` — presence/named sessions survive every sweep shape (property test over generated trees).

### Edge / border cases

- **E3** — clock skew / mtime touch by backup tools → last-used falls back to header `updatedAt` when mtime < header time.

- **E5** — `sweep: off` with cap set: manual verb still works, boot never sweeps (only the over-cap note).
- **E6** — cross-slug fairness: cap is global across all project slugs; no slug starvation (oldest wins globally).

## Non-goals

  stays a `cookie:` header (not Bearer) and the JWT keeps its Bearer
  slot. Every add/connect flow that saves a
  registry entry offers a provider-name step (`_askConnectProviderName`:
  typed value, else the endpoint host; a clash with a DIFFERENT endpoint
  retries, and so does a name matching a CATALOG provider — `/provider
  kimi` routes to the catalog before the registry lookup, so such an
  entry would be unreachable) — the custom wizard, DIAL (custom names
  scope the store key; the switch stores under the entry's slot via
  `tokenKeyName`), Kimi (a typed key becomes a named
  entry with a name-scoped key; a resolved key offers "use it / add a
  second account"), OpenRouter OAuth + API-key, ChatGPT OAuth (lands a
  registry entry too, `apiType: chatgpt`; ONE identity per auth domain —
  issue #1706: a second codex/chatgpt auth lands ON the resolved
  same-domain record, a typed new name RENAMES it instead of minting a
  twin, and the load merge folds any codex records that already exist —
  so `/provider` lists the ChatGPT account exactly once, however it is
  named), CodeMie SSO/JWT (the
  SSO name step only from the explicit add flows: `offerName` — automatic
  re-authorizations on startup/switch/mid-stream expiry stay silent; a
  NEW account name re-runs the guided project → model pick, a re-login
  to the same entry keeps its model).
  Saved-entry lookups are by base URL (`_entryForBaseUrl`), so a renamed
  entry is not duplicated on re-connect. Catalog switches RESET
  `_activeCustomName` (kimi/openrouter stored-key branches included) —
  a leaked marker made `/model` rewrite the previous custom entry's
  model memory. `/models` also manages
  the `models:` section: `/models config`/`set <slot> <model> [baseUrl]`/
  `remove <slot>` for media slot overrides (persisted via
  `onModelsConfigChanged`), and `/model <name>` resolves `models.custom`
  definitions. Keys: env first, then
  secure store (`lib/src/secrets/secure_key_store*.dart` — Keychain /
  Secret Service / PasswordVault, IO backends only in `lib/io.dart`),
  preloaded into `SecureKeyCache`. Resolution: the spec's DEFAULT endpoint
  gets env → `FA_KEY_<HOST>` → `FA_KEY_<HOST>_<NAME>` → legacy; any other
  endpoint resolves ONLY its scoped store keys (env names never hijack a
  custom endpoint); `/key set` writes store-only, never config.
  `/settings` is the interactive settings hub: a TUI picker whose entries
  (Provider, Edit/delete provider, Chat model, Model parameters, Media
  models, Agent models, Approval mode, Agent mode, API keys, MCP servers)
  launch the same flows the dedicated slash commands open; line mode prints
  a summary. ALL TUI pickers (generic host pickers included) have
  type-to-filter + backspace (generic ones filter their static item list
  locally via `menuAllItems`, the models picker rebuilds through
  `buildModelMenu`; a no-match filter keeps the title + `(no matches)`).
  The `/model` TUI menu is TWO-STEP when several providers exist:
  `_buildModelMenu` returns provider rows (`@<name>` keys, the filter
  matches provider names AND their model ids) first, and selecting one
  opens that provider's model list (generic `modelProvider` picker whose
  `provider|model` rows route back through `_tuiSelectModel`'s
  cross-provider switch). A single provider goes straight to its models.
  Model rows render as a TABLE (`buildModelPickerTable` in
  `model_picker_table.dart`): `● id  provider  ctx  cost` with the
  context window compacted (1048576 → `1M`) and `$/Mtok` from the catalog
  (`—` when pricing is unknown, never 0.00); rows sort recency → cheaper
  total → unpriced last; narrow widths elide cost first, then provider,
  keeping id + ctx. The rows are click targets (hit-region routing).
  The provider→model pick flows live in `lib/src/cli/settings_flow.dart` in the
  NAMED `SettingsFlow` extension (public `runProviderModelFlow`/
  `startChatModelFlow`/`startMediaSlotFlow`/`startAgentModelFlow`), so
  tests can drive them line-mode (see `test/cli/settings_flow_test.dart`).
  The model-list fetch dispatches per dialect
  (`_fetchProviderModelIds`: CodeMie `/llm_models` by URL marker, DIAL
  deployments when the spec is `dial`, the Codex backend `/models` for
  the chatgpt-codex kind — the same call codex-rs' models-manager makes,
  with the bundled synced catalog (`chatGptCodexModels`,
  `scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`) answering offline — else OpenAI
  `/models`; the saved entry's own key authenticates; failures fall back
  to manual entry; the `/model` picker's per-entry cache refresh
  (`_fetchIdsForProvider`) shares the same dispatch so a saved codex
  entry lists the whole catalog, not just its last-used model).
  `startAgentModelFlow` pins the `smol`/`subagent` role chains through
  `ModelRolesResolver.setRoleChain`/`clearRoleChain` (the resolver is
  created on demand when the config had no `roles:` section —
  `AgentCliConfig.modelRolesResolver` is mutable) and persists via
  `onModelsConfigChanged` (bin/fah.dart's persistConfig reads the live
  resolver config).
- `lib/src/cube/` — fa_cube sandbox profiles (issue #8): strict `CubeSpec`
  YAML (`.fah/cubes/<name>.yaml`, apiVersion fa/v1 kind Cube) with
  tool/network/fs/env/resource/cache policies (deny-wins, empty allowlist =
  deny-all, lexical path normalization as traversal guard), `CubeResolver`
  (path > name lookup), Dart-layer enforcement (`SandboxedExecutionEnv`
  decorator: `CubeFsGuard` gates the agent's own read/edit/write tools,
  `CubePolicyEngine` gates bash incl. pipes/`$(...)` subshells and shell
  redirect targets (`>`/`>>`/`<>`/`&>`/`2>` writes, `<` reads, `2>&1`
  exempt; arguments stay name-gated only), exit 127
  denials with per-exec reason), content-addressed `CubeCacheManager` under
  `.fah/cube-cache/<md5>/` (manifest + ttl). `spec.backend:` = `policy`
  (default, Dart-only) | `kernel` opt-in: every command wrapped in the OS
  sandbox via `CubeSandboxBackend.wrapCommand` — macOS `sandbox-exec -f
  <profile>`, Linux `unshare --user --map-root-user --mount [--net iff the
  spec allows no network]` + `ulimit -v/-t` ceilings, both over a clean
  `env -i` environment; profiles staged content-verified under

# gh-1746: [GOAL] Session disk hygiene: opt-in retention cap + age-aware sweep (nothing auto-deleted unless configured)

## Description

## Goal — Session disk hygiene (v2 — revised framing)

One sentence: **the sessions root gets an opt-in retention policy (`sessions.retention`) — a total-size cap enforced by an age-aware, live/named-safe sweep at boot — so a workspace of marathon sessions can never quietly eat the disk, while with no config nothing is EVER auto-deleted.**

Today nothing bounds the sessions root: a single marathon workspace holds 425 MB + 4.8 GB transcripts (measured, dmtools slug), macOS has already throttled fa for 8.6 GB of dirty writes in 15 h (YuryBY's #1745 diag log). The only tools are manual: `fa session repair` shrinks a ledger, `delete` removes one session, `cleanupEmptySessions` removes EMPTY files. There is no cap, no sweep, no usage visibility beyond `/sessions` listing.

## Why this framing

- **v1 of this issue ("configurable full-open bound") is RETRACTED as the framing** — it answered a memory-risk question (how big a file may be fully opened), not the owner's actual ask (stop sessions filling the disk). The full-open knob stays a legitimate second-tier follow-up, listed under Non-goals.
- "Auto-clean by default" is rejected as the default posture: silently deleting session history is the one irreversible action fa must never take unconfigured. Opt-in cap (variant B below) is the recommendation; the alternative (default cap) is an explicit open question for the owner.

## Architecture

Named components:

- **Config** (user file, tolerant section — unknown keys note, never boot-fail):
  ```yaml
  sessions:
    retention:
      maxTotalBytes: 0      # 0/absent = NO cap, nothing is ever auto-deleted (default)
      minAgeDays: 14        # a session younger than this is never swept
      keepNamed: true       # named sessions (--session <name>) are always exempt
      sweep: boot           # boot | off — when the sweep runs (off = cap set but manual-only)
  ```
- **Usage walk** — O(directory entries), never O(file bytes): stat-based size + last-used (mtime; a live presence marker overrides recency), reusing the header-only listing the picker already streams.
- **Sweep** (`SessionRetentionSweeper`, pure-Dart core over `ExecutionEnv`): when total > `maxTotalBytes`, delete oldest-last-used first until under the cap, skipping: live sessions (presence file), named sessions (`keepNamed`), anything younger than `minAgeDays`, and the CURRENT session. Every deletion logs one line (file, size, age, reason). If the exempt set alone exceeds the cap, STOP and emit a loud note naming the blockers — never force.
- **Session-owned artifacts die with the session**: the transcript JSONL plus its sidecars in the same sweep unit — `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml`, `spills/<sessionId>/`, trajectory blobs `<sid>/`. Presence files are garbage-collected separately (they are not user data; #1660/#1740 already touched them).
- **Visibility**: `/sessions` gains a usage footer (`total X GB across N sessions, cap Y`); `fa sessions clean [--dry-run]` runs the sweep manually with a full report (what would be / was deleted, freed bytes, exemptions).
- Degradation: absent section = byte-identical today; a cap set but unreachable exemptions = note, no deletion loop.

## Capability surface

| Surface | Today | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Total disk cap | none | `maxTotalBytes`, opt-in |
| Auto-delete | none (manual delete only) | boot sweep, oldest-first, exempt live/named/young |
| Manual verb | `fa session repair`, per-file delete | `fa sessions clean --dry-run` + apply |
| Usage visibility | `/sessions` list only | total + per-slug + cap footer |
| Sidecar cleanup | none | dies with its session |

Tiering: **core** = config + sweeper + `fa sessions clean` + `/sessions` footer; **second tier** = app Settings surface, Trash-style archive instead of delete (`retention.archive: true` moves to `.fah/trash/`); **excluded** — spills/bash-jobs GLOBAL caps (their own growth has separate cards; only session-scoped subdirs ride this sweep), and any compaction of LIVE sessions (repair owns that).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — no `sessions:` section → no sweep ever runs, no boot note (byte-identical legacy; UT on config).
- **AC2** — cap set, total under → no deletions (UT).
- **AC3** — cap set, total over → oldest-last-used deleted until under; deleted set excludes live (presence), named (`keepNamed: true`), younger than `minAgeDays`, and the current session (IT with fake fs + fake clock).
- **AC4** — exempt-only overflow: nothing deleted, loud note names each blocker with size (UT).
- **AC5** — deleting a session removes its sidecars (`.tools/`, `spills/<sid>/`, trajectory blobs) in the same unit (IT).
- **AC6** — `fa sessions clean --dry-run` prints the exact plan (paths, sizes, ages, reasons) and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly the plan (E2E).
- **AC7** — every auto-deletion emits one log line; a sweep report persists to the boot log (IT asserts the lines).

## Test plan

- `UT-1..2` — config parse (absent/invalid/zero/valid) → AC1/2.
- `UT-3` — sweeper selection order + exemptions on a synthetic tree (AC3/4).
- `IT-1` — fake `ExecutionEnv` + fake clock: full sweep lifecycle incl. sidecars (AC3/5), log lines (AC7).
- `IT-2` — named/live/young exemption matrix (AC3).
- `E2E-1` — real fs temp root: `fa sessions clean --dry-run` then apply; `/sessions` footer numbers (AC6).
- `REG-1` **merge-blocking**: legacy-config fixture (no section) — no sweep, no notes, `/sessions` output byte-identical modulo the new footer line being ABSENT without a cap. **A red REG-1 job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**
- `REG-2` — presence/named sessions survive every sweep shape (property test over generated trees).

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — cap smaller than one marathon session: that session is still a deletion candidate (oldest-first) unless exempt — minAgeDays is the guard, not size.
- **E2** — race: a session becomes live mid-sweep → presence check immediately before each unlink; skip on mismatch.
- **E3** — clock skew / mtime touch by backup tools → last-used falls back to header `updatedAt` when mtime < header time.
- **E4** — symlinked session root: never follow links out of the root (path-escape test).
- **E5** — `sweep: off` with cap set: manual verb still works, boot never sweeps (only the over-cap note).
- **E6** — cross-slug fairness: cap is global across all project slugs; no slug starvation (oldest wins globally).

## Non-goals

- No default cap / no surprise deletion ever (that is the framing, restated as a guarantee).
- No live-session compaction/repair inside the sweep (`fa session repair` owns shrinking).
- No spills/bash-jobs global quotas — session-scoped subdirs only.
- The retracted v1 full-open knob (`sessions.maxFullOpenBytes`) — separate follow-up if wanted.
- No cloud/archive backend.

## Open questions

1. Default posture: **B (recommended)** — no cap unless set, boot NOTE (no action) when total crosses a soft warn threshold (e.g. 5 GiB) suggesting the keys; or **A** — ship a generous default cap (e.g. 20 GiB) with the same exemptions, so hygiene exists out of the box. Owner decides.
2. Delete vs archive-to-`.fah/trash/` for auto-swept sessions (manual verb always hard-deletes): recommend archive as second tier, delete for core.

## References

- Measured: dmtools slug 425 MB live + 4.8 GB kimi transcript; macOS throttle diag in #1745.
- Code: `session_repo.dart:413` (`cleanupEmptySessions` — empties only), `session_commands.dart` (manual delete), no retention anywhere (`grep retention|prune` — nothing).
- Related: #1745 (ledger growth — the producer side; this card is the consumer side), gh-1073/#1247 (per-record caps), #1590/#1594 (snapshot ledgers), #919 (bash_jobs log growth — adjacent, excluded here).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions

{

    "summary": "[GOAL] Session disk hygiene: opt-in retention cap + age-aware sweep (nothing auto-deleted unless configured)",
    "description": "## Goal — Session disk hygiene (v2 — revised framing)

One sentence: **the sessions root gets an opt-in retention policy (`sessions.retention`) — a total-size cap enforced by an age-aware, live/named-safe sweep at boot — so a workspace of marathon sessions can never quietly eat the disk, while with no config nothing is EVER auto-deleted.**

Today nothing bounds the sessions root: a single marathon workspace holds 425 MB + 4.8 GB transcripts (measured, dmtools slug), macOS has already throttled fa for 8.6 GB of dirty writes in 15 h (YuryBY's #1745 diag log). The only tools are manual: `fa session repair` shrinks a ledger, `delete` removes one session, `cleanupEmptySessions` removes EMPTY files. There is no cap, no sweep, no usage visibility beyond `/sessions` listing.

## Why this framing

- **v1 of this issue ("configurable full-open bound") is RETRACTED as the framing** — it answered a memory-risk question (how big a file may be fully opened), not the owner's actual ask (stop sessions filling the disk). The full-open knob stays a legitimate second-tier follow-up, listed under Non-goals.
- "Auto-clean by default" is rejected as the default posture: silently deleting session history is the one irreversible action fa must never take unconfigured. Opt-in cap (variant B below) is the recommendation; the alternative (default cap) is an explicit open question for the owner.

## Architecture

Named components:

- **Config** (user file, tolerant section — unknown keys note, never boot-fail):
  ```yaml
  sessions:
    retention:
      maxTotalBytes: 0      # 0/absent = NO cap, nothing is ever auto-deleted (default)
      minAgeDays: 14        # a session younger than this is never swept
      keepNamed: true       # named sessions (--session <name>) are always exempt
      sweep: boot           # boot | off — when the sweep runs (off = cap set but manual-only)
  ```
- **Usage walk** — O(directory entries), never O(file bytes): stat-based size + last-used (mtime; a live presence marker overrides recency), reusing the header-only listing the picker already streams.
- **Sweep** (`SessionRetentionSweeper`, pure-Dart core over `ExecutionEnv`): when total > `maxTotalBytes`, delete oldest-last-used first until under the cap, skipping: live sessions (presence file), named sessions (`keepNamed`), anything younger than `minAgeDays`, and the CURRENT session. Every deletion logs one line (file, size, age, reason). If the exempt set alone exceeds the cap, STOP and emit a loud note naming the blockers — never force.
- **Session-owned artifacts die with the session**: the transcript JSONL plus its sidecars in the same sweep unit — `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml`, `spills/<sessionId>/`, trajectory blobs `<sid>/`. Presence files are garbage-collected separately (they are not user data; #1660/#1740 already touched them).
- **Visibility**: `/sessions` gains a usage footer (`total X GB across N sessions, cap Y`); `fa sessions clean [--dry-run]` runs the sweep manually with a full report (what would be / was deleted, freed bytes, exemptions).
- Degradation: absent section = byte-identical today; a cap set but unreachable exemptions = note, no deletion loop.

## Capability surface

| Surface | Today | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Total disk cap | none | `maxTotalBytes`, opt-in |
| Auto-delete | none (manual delete only) | boot sweep, oldest-first, exempt live/named/young |
| Manual verb | `fa session repair`, per-file delete | `fa sessions clean --dry-run` + apply |
| Usage visibility | `/sessions` list only | total + per-slug + cap footer |
| Sidecar cleanup | none | dies with its session |

Tiering: **core** = config + sweeper + `fa sessions clean` + `/sessions` footer; **second tier** = app Settings surface, Trash-style archive instead of delete (`retention.archive: true` moves to `.fah/trash/`); **excluded** — spills/bash-jobs GLOBAL caps (their own growth has separate cards; only session-scoped subdirs ride this sweep), and any compaction of LIVE sessions (repair owns that).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — no `sessions:` section → no sweep ever runs, no boot note (byte-identical legacy; UT on config).
- **AC2** — cap set, total under → no deletions (UT).
- **AC3** — cap set, total over → oldest-last-used deleted until under; deleted set excludes live (presence), named (`keepNamed: true`), younger than `minAgeDays`, and the current session (IT with fake fs + fake clock).
- **AC4** — exempt-only overflow: nothing deleted, loud note names each blocker with size (UT).
- **AC5** — deleting a session removes its sidecars (`.tools/`, `spills/<sid>/`, trajectory blobs) in the same unit (IT).
- **AC6** — `fa sessions clean --dry-run` prints the exact plan (paths, sizes, ages, reasons) and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly the plan (E2E).
- **AC7** — every auto-deletion emits one log line; a sweep report persists to the boot log (IT asserts the lines).

## Test plan

- `UT-1..2` — config parse (absent/invalid/zero/valid) → AC1/2.
- `UT-3` — sweeper selection order + exemptions on a synthetic tree (AC3/4).
- `IT-1` — fake `ExecutionEnv` + fake clock: full sweep lifecycle incl. sidecars (AC3/5), log lines (AC7).
- `IT-2` — named/live/young exemption matrix (AC3).
- `E2E-1` — real fs temp root: `fa sessions clean --dry-run` then apply; `/sessions` footer numbers (AC6).
- `REG-1` **merge-blocking**: legacy-config fixture (no section) — no sweep, no notes, `/sessions` output byte-identical modulo the new footer line being ABSENT without a cap. **A red REG-1 job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**
- `REG-2` — presence/named sessions survive every sweep shape (property test over generated trees).

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — cap smaller than one marathon session: that session is still a deletion candidate (oldest-first) unless exempt — minAgeDays is the guard, not size.
- **E2** — race: a session becomes live mid-sweep → presence check immediately before each unlink; skip on mismatch.
- **E3** — clock skew / mtime touch by backup tools → last-used falls back to header `updatedAt` when mtime < header time.
- **E4** — symlinked session root: never follow links out of the root (path-escape test).
- **E5** — `sweep: off` with cap set: manual verb still works, boot never sweeps (only the over-cap note).
- **E6** — cross-slug fairness: cap is global across all project slugs; no slug starvation (oldest wins globally).

## Non-goals

- No default cap / no surprise deletion ever (that is the framing, restated as a guarantee).
- No live-session compaction/repair inside the sweep (`fa session repair` owns shrinking).
- No spills/bash-jobs global quotas — session-scoped subdirs only.
- The retracted v1 full-open knob (`sessions.maxFullOpenBytes`) — separate follow-up if wanted.
- No cloud/archive backend.

## Open questions

1. Default posture: **B (recommended)** — no cap unless set, boot NOTE (no action) when total crosses a soft warn threshold (e.g. 5 GiB) suggesting the keys; or **A** — ship a generous default cap (e.g. 20 GiB) with the same exemptions, so hygiene exists out of the box. Owner decides.
2. Delete vs archive-to-`.fah/trash/` for auto-swept sessions (manual verb always hard-deletes): recommend archive as second tier, delete for core.

- Measured: dmtools slug 425 MB live + 4.8 GB kimi transcript; macOS throttle diag in #1745.

{
  "key": "gh-1746",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "[GOAL] Session disk hygiene: opt-in retention cap + age-aware sweep (nothing auto-deleted unless configured)",
    "description": "## Goal — Session disk hygiene (v2 — revised framing)

One sentence: **the sessions root gets an opt-in retention policy (`sessions.retention`) — a total-size cap enforced by an age-aware, live/named-safe sweep at boot — so a workspace of marathon sessions can never quietly eat the disk, while with no config nothing is EVER auto-deleted.**

Today nothing bounds the sessions root: a single marathon workspace holds 425 MB + 4.8 GB transcripts (measured, dmtools slug), macOS has already throttled fa for 8.6 GB of dirty writes in 15 h (YuryBY's #1745 diag log). The only tools are manual: `fa session repair` shrinks a ledger, `delete` removes one session, `cleanupEmptySessions` removes EMPTY files. There is no cap, no sweep, no usage visibility beyond `/sessions` listing.

## Why this framing

- **v1 of this issue ("configurable full-open bound") is RETRACTED as the framing** — it answered a memory-risk question (how big a file may be fully opened), not the owner's actual ask (stop sessions filling the disk). The full-open knob stays a legitimate second-tier follow-up, listed under Non-goals.
- "Auto-clean by default" is rejected as the default posture: silently deleting session history is the one irreversible action fa must never take unconfigured. Opt-in cap (variant B below) is the recommendation; the alternative (default cap) is an explicit open question for the owner.

## Architecture

Named components:

- **Config** (user file, tolerant section — unknown keys note, never boot-fail):
  ```yaml
  sessions:
    retention:
      maxTotalBytes: 0      # 0/absent = NO cap, nothing is ever auto-deleted (default)
      minAgeDays: 14        # a session younger than this is never swept
      keepNamed: true       # named sessions (--session <name>) are always exempt
      sweep: boot           # boot | off — when the sweep runs (off = cap set but manual-only)
  ```
- **Usage walk** — O(directory entries), never O(file bytes): stat-based size + last-used (mtime; a live presence marker overrides recency), reusing the header-only listing the picker already streams.
- **Sweep** (`SessionRetentionSweeper`, pure-Dart core over `ExecutionEnv`): when total > `maxTotalBytes`, delete oldest-last-used first until under the cap, skipping: live sessions (presence file), named sessions (`keepNamed`), anything younger than `minAgeDays`, and the CURRENT session. Every deletion logs one line (file, size, age, reason). If the exempt set alone exceeds the cap, STOP and emit a loud note naming the blockers — never force.
- **Session-owned artifacts die with the session**: the transcript JSONL plus its sidecars in the same sweep unit — `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml`, `spills/<sessionId>/`, trajectory blobs `<sid>/`. Presence files are garbage-collected separately (they are not user data; #1660/#1740 already touched them).
- **Visibility**: `/sessions` gains a usage footer (`total X GB across N sessions, cap Y`); `fa sessions clean [--dry-run]` runs the sweep manually with a full report (what would be / was deleted, freed bytes, exemptions).
- Degradation: absent section = byte-identical today; a cap set but unreachable exemptions = note, no deletion loop.

## Capability surface

| Surface | Today | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Total disk cap | none | `maxTotalBytes`, opt-in |
| Auto-delete | none (manual delete only) | boot sweep, oldest-first, exempt live/named/young |
| Manual verb | `fa session repair`, per-file delete | `fa sessions clean --dry-run` + apply |
| Usage visibility | `/sessions` list only | total + per-slug + cap footer |
| Sidecar cleanup | none | dies with its session |

Tiering: **core** = config + sweeper + `fa sessions clean` + `/sessions` footer; **second tier** = app Settings surface, Trash-style archive instead of delete (`retention.archive: true` moves to `.fah/trash/`); **excluded** — spills/bash-jobs GLOBAL caps (their own growth has separate cards; only session-scoped subdirs ride this sweep), and any compaction of LIVE sessions (repair owns that).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — no `sessions:` section → no sweep ever runs, no boot note (byte-identical legacy; UT on config).
- **AC2** — cap set, total under → no deletions (UT).
- **AC3** — cap set, total over → oldest-last-used deleted until under; deleted set excludes live (presence), named (`keepNamed: true`), younger than `minAgeDays`, and the current session (IT with fake fs + fake clock).
- **AC4** — exempt-only overflow: nothing deleted, loud note names each blocker with size (UT).
- **AC5** — deleting a session removes its sidecars (`.tools/`, `spills/<sid>/`, trajectory blobs) in the same unit (IT).
- **AC6** — `fa sessions clean --dry-run` prints the exact plan (paths, sizes, ages, reasons) and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly the plan (E2E).
- **AC7** — every auto-deletion emits one log line; a sweep report persists to the boot log (IT asserts the lines).

## Test plan

- `UT-1..2` — config parse (absent/invalid/zero/valid) → AC1/2.
- `UT-3` — sweeper selection order + exemptions on a synthetic tree (AC3/4).
- `IT-1` — fake `ExecutionEnv` + fake clock: full sweep lifecycle incl. sidecars (AC3/5), log lines (AC7).
- `IT-2` — named/live/young exemption matrix (AC3).
- `E2E-1` — real fs temp root: `fa sessions clean --dry-run` then apply; `/sessions` footer numbers (AC6).
- `REG-1` **merge-blocking**: legacy-config fixture (no section) — no sweep, no notes, `/sessions` output byte-identical modulo the new footer line being ABSENT without a cap. **A red REG-1 job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**
- `REG-2` — presence/named sessions survive every sweep shape (property test over generated trees).

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — cap smaller than one marathon session: that session is still a deletion candidate (oldest-first) unless exempt — minAgeDays is the guard, not size.
- **E2** — race: a session becomes live mid-sweep → presence check immediately before each unlink; skip on mismatch.
- **E3** — clock skew / mtime touch by backup tools → last-used falls back to header `updatedAt` when mtime < header time.
- **E4** — symlinked session root: never follow links out of the root (path-escape test).
- **E5** — `sweep: off` with cap set: manual verb still works, boot never sweeps (only the over-cap note).
- **E6** — cross-slug fairness: cap is global across all project slugs; no slug starvation (oldest wins globally).

## Non-goals

- No default cap / no surprise deletion ever (that is the framing, restated as a guarantee).
- No live-session compaction/repair inside the sweep (`fa session repair` owns shrinking).
- No spills/bash-jobs global quotas — session-scoped subdirs only.
- The retracted v1 full-open knob (`sessions.maxFullOpenBytes`) — separate follow-up if wanted.
- No cloud/archive backend.

## Open questions

1. Default posture: **B (recommended)** — no cap unless set, boot NOTE (no action) when total crosses a soft warn threshold (e.g. 5 GiB) suggesting the keys; or **A** — ship a generous default cap (e.g. 20 GiB) with the same exemptions, so hygiene exists out of the box. Owner decides.
2. Delete vs archive-to-`.fah/trash/` for auto-swept sessions (manual verb always hard-deletes): recommend archive as second tier, delete for core.

## References

- Measured: dmtools slug 425 MB live + 4.8 GB kimi transcript; macOS throttle diag in #1745.
- Code: `session_repo.dart:413` (`cleanupEmptySessions` — empties only), `session_commands.dart` (manual delete), no retention anywhere (`grep retention|prune` — nothing).
- Related: #1745 (ledger growth — the producer side; this card is the consumer side), gh-1073/#1247 (per-record caps), #1590/#1594 (snapshot ledgers), #919 (bash_jobs log growth — adjacent, excluded here)."
  }
}

static int _intWithNote(
    Object? value,
    int fallback,
    String name,
    List<String> notes,
  ) {
    if (value is int) return value;
    if (value is num) return value.round();
    notes.add('$name: not a number, default applied');
    return fallback;
  }
}

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not
/// empty/whitespace (issue #678 AC1 boundary both sides, AC2 empty
/// never spills). Pure function.
bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;
  // Empty / whitespace-only results never spill (AC2).
  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;
  return text.length > config.threshold;
}

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not
/// empty/whitespace (issue #678 AC1 boundary both sides, AC2 empty
/// never spills). Pure function.
bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;

  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not
/// empty/whitespace (issue #678 AC1 boundary both sides, AC2 empty
/// never spills). Pure function.
bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;
  // Empty / whitespace-only results never spill (AC2).
  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;
  return text.length > config.threshold;

static int _intWithNote(
    Object? value,
    int fallback,
    String name,
    List<String> notes,
  ) {
    if (value is int) return value;
    if (value is num) return value.round();
    notes.add('$name: not a number, default applied');
    return fallback;
  }
}

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not
/// empty/whitespace (issue #678 AC1 boundary both sides, AC2 empty
/// never spills). Pure function.
bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;
  // Empty / whitespace-only results never spill (AC2).
  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;
  return text.length > config.threshold;
}

static int _intWithNote(
    Object? value,
    int fallback,
    String name,
    List<String> notes,
  ) {
    if (value is int) return value;
    if (value is num) return value.round();
    notes.add('$name: not a number, default applied');
    return fallback;
  }
}

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not
/// empty/whitespace (issue #678 AC1 boundary both sides, AC2 empty
/// never spills). Pure function.
bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;
  // Empty / whitespace-only results never spill (AC2).
  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;
  return text.length > config.threshold;
}

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not

bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;
  // Empty / whitespace-only results never spill (AC2).
  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;
  return text.length > config.threshold;

    Object? value,

    String name,
    List<String> notes,

    if (value is int) return value;
    if (value is num) return value.round();

  }

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not
/// empty/whitespace (issue #678 AC1 boundary both sides, AC2 empty
/// never spills). Pure function.
bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;
  // Empty / whitespace-only results never spill (AC2).
  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;
  return text.length > config.threshold;
}

static int _intWithNote(
    Object? value,
    int fallback,
    String name,
    List<String> notes,
  ) {
    if (value is int) return value;
    if (value is num) return value.round();
    notes.add('$name: not a number, default applied');
    return fallback;
  }
}

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not
/// empty/whitespace (issue #678 AC1 boundary both sides, AC2 empty
/// never spills). Pure function.
bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;
  // Empty / whitespace-only results never spill (AC2).
  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;
  return text.length > config.threshold;
}

static int _intWithNote(
    Object? value,
    int fallback,
    String name,
    List<String> notes,
  ) {
    if (value is int) return value;
    if (value is num) return value.round();
    notes.add('$name: not a number, default applied');
    return fallback;
  }
}

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not
/// empty/whitespace (issue #678 AC1 boundary both sides, AC2 empty
/// never spills). Pure function.
bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;
  // Empty / whitespace-only results never spill (AC2).
  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;
  return text.length > config.threshold;
}

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not
/// empty/whitespace (issue #678 AC1 boundary both sides, AC2 empty
/// never spills). Pure function.
bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;
  // Empty / whitespace-only results never spill (AC2).
  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;
  return text.length > config.threshold;
}

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not
/// empty/whitespace (issue #678 AC1 boundary both sides, AC2 empty
/// never spills). Pure function.
bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;
  // Empty / whitespace-only results never spill (AC2).
  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;
  return text.length > config.threshold;
}

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not
/// empty/whitespace (issue #678 AC1 boundary both sides, AC2 empty
/// never spills). Pure function.
bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;
  // Empty / whitespace-only results never spill (AC2).
  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;
  return text.length > config.threshold;
}

static int _intWithNote(
    Object? value,
    int fallback,
    String name,

    if (value is int) return value;
    if (value is num) return value.round();

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not
/// empty/whitespace (issue #678 AC1 boundary both sides, AC2 empty
/// never spills). Pure function.
bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;
  // Empty / whitespace-only results never spill (AC2).
  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;
  return text.length > config.threshold;
}

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not
/// empty/whitespace (issue #678 AC1 boundary both sides, AC2 empty
/// never spills). Pure function.
bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;
  // Empty / whitespace-only results never spill (AC2).
  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;
  return text.length > config.threshold;
}

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not
/// empty/whitespace (issue #678 AC1 boundary both sides, AC2 empty
/// never spills). Pure function.
bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;
  // Empty / whitespace-only results never spill (AC2).
  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;
  return text.length > config.threshold;
}

    if (value is int) return value;
    if (value is num) return value.round();

  }

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not
/// empty/whitespace (issue #678 AC1 boundary both sides, AC2 empty
/// never spills). Pure function.
bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;
  // Empty / whitespace-only results never spill (AC2).
  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;
  return text.length > config.threshold;
}

static int _intWithNote(
    Object? value,
    int fallback,
    String name,
    List<String> notes,
  ) {
    if (value is int) return value;
    if (value is num) return value.round();

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not
/// empty/whitespace (issue #678 AC1 boundary both sides, AC2 empty
/// never spills). Pure function.
bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;
  // Empty / whitespace-only results never spill (AC2).
  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;
  return text.length > config.threshold;
}

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not
/// empty/whitespace (issue #678 AC1 boundary both sides, AC2 empty
/// never spills). Pure function.
bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;
  // Empty / whitespace-only results never spill (AC2).
  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;
  return text.length > config.threshold;
}

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not

bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;
  // Empty / whitespace-only results never spill (AC2).
  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;

static int _intWithNote(
    Object? value,
    int fallback,
    String name,
    List<String> notes,
  ) {
    if (value is int) return value;
    if (value is num) return value.round();
    notes.add('$name: not a number, default applied');
    return fallback;
  }
}

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not
/// empty/whitespace (issue #678 AC1 boundary both sides, AC2 empty
/// never spills). Pure function.
bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;
  // Empty / whitespace-only results never spill (AC2).
  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;
  return text.length > config.threshold;
}

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not

bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;
  // Empty / whitespace-only results never spill (AC2).
  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;
  return text.length > config.threshold;

/// True when [text] spills: longer than the threshold and not
/// empty/whitespace (issue #678 AC1 boundary both sides, AC2 empty
/// never spills). Pure function.
bool shouldSpill(String text, SpillsConfig config) {
  // Kill-switch / zero threshold = legacy: nothing ever spills (AC1).
  if (!config.isActive) return false;
  // Empty / whitespace-only results never spill (AC2).
  if (text.trim().isEmpty) return false;
  return text.length > config.threshold;
}

Hmm, no: Dart 3.6/3.7 introduced the wildcard variables; private named parameters landed in Dart 3.10 as an experiment? Actually "private named parameters" (`this._x` in constructors) shipped in Dart 3.10? Let me not risk it — I used `_spillFreed: 0` as a named arg. If the language version doesn't support it, compile error. Simpler: drop the field entirely; compute remainingBytes = totalBytes - freedBytes + spillAdjust... Actually simplest: store `rootFreedBytes` (root-side only) and compute freedBytes = rootFreed + spillFreed for display. Then remainingBytes = totalBytes - rootFreed. Config GREEN. Now the sweper tests (RED). Write `test/session_retention_test.dart` — the sweper over MemoryExecutionEnv with a fake clock, presence store, seeding via JsonlSessionRepo.

Key test fixture decisions:
- `MemoryExecutionEnv(cwd: '/work')`, sessionsRoot '/sessions'.
- Clock: `DateTime Function()` fixed `now = DateTime(2026, 1, 10, 12)`.
- Seed helper: create session via repo, append content to grow size, setMtime backdated.
- Presence: `FileSessionPresenceStore(env: env, root: '/sessions', now: clock, staleAfter: ...)` — needs freshness vs fake clock: register() writes touchedAt=now() (fake) and list() compares vs same clock → fresh. 

Careful: FileSessionPresenceStore.cleanupAfter default & the gh-1660 sweep-dead-files with pidAlive null — a fresh row stays. Good.

Wait — one problem: FileSessionPresenceStore constructor takes `DateTime Function()? now` — yes injectable.

- Names: `await session.appendSessionName('keepme')` — writes a record; tail probe reads it.

Sweper usage counts bytes: MemoryFileSystem FileInfo.size = written bytes. The JSONL file after create = header line (~150 bytes). Appending content grows it. setMtime overrides mtime — but does MemoryFileSystem keep size? setMtime replaces `_MemoryFile(file.bytes, mtimeMs)` — keeps bytes. Good.

For spill dirs: `env.writeFile('/work/.fah/spills/<sid>/1.txt', 'x')` — the seeded session's header cwd = '/work' (the repo create cwd) — matches MemoryExecutionEnv cwd... The header cwd is what I pass to create (cwd: '/work'). Sweper spill path = `<headerCwd>/.fah/spills/<sid>`. Absolute path fine for MemoryFileSystem.

For the usage dir: gh-1241 layout `<root>/<sid>/usage.json` — write directly: `env.writeFile('/sessions/<sid>/usage.json', ...)`.

Sizes: make deterministic bytes (e.g. 'x' * N). Total = headerSize + N + sidecars. Cap arithmetic: to force "delete oldest until under cap", pick caps relative to measured sizes rather than absolutes: e.g. read usage() first, then choose cap. But sweper computes usage internally each sweep — cap passed via retention config fixed at construction. Simpler: craft sizes so totals are predictable: header line length is deterministic but annoying; instead assert RELATIVE behavior:
- Create 4 sessions A(old,300B) B(old,300B) C(young) D(named).
- Backdate A/B mtimes (old), C mtime recent, D old but named.
- retention: maxTotalBytes = <total - 350> so deleting the oldest single unit (~header+300+...) brings it under. Assert exactly [A] deleted (oldest), B/C/D kept. Then another test with tighter cap deletes A then B (order asserted).

Deterministic assertions via relative caps are robust. For "under cap → nothing (AC2)": cap = huge.

Test list (unit/IT in one file, groups):

group 'usage walk':
 1. counts units: primaries + parts + corupt + .tools yaml + usage dir; ignores .trash, .presence, messages dir, non-jsonl files.
 2. spillBytes measured, NOT in total.
 3. E3 mtime floor.

group 'plan/apply (AC2/AC3/AC4)':
 4. AC2 under cap → no deletions.
 5. oldest-first selection until under cap; current/live/young/named exempted (AC3).
 6. keepNamed: false → named deletable.
 7. AC4 exempt-only overflow: blockers named w/ sizes, no deletions.
 8. E1 cap smaller than one marathon session: still deletable.

group 'apply deletes units (AC5) + logs (AC7)':
 9. apply removes primary + parts + corupt + .tools/<sid>.yaml + usage dir + spills dir; log lines one per deletion; freed bytes.
 10. E2 live mid-sweep skip.

group 'boot policy':
 11. enforceAtBoot no-cap + over soft warn → overSoftWarn (and below → silent).
 12. cap + sweep off + over → overCapSweepOff, no deletions (E5).
 13. E6 cross-slug fairness: two slug dirs, oldest across slugs wins.
 14. E4 path escape: header sid with '..' (write a session file whose basename sid is safe but header id evil — hmm, my unit keys off BASENAME sid. The header-sid escape applies to usage dir joins: usageDirsByName keyed by TOP-LEVEL DIR NAME (safe basenames) — the join `<root>/<sid>` uses basename-derived sid (safe). Spill join uses header cwd + basename sid. So the escape guard: isSafePathSegment(basename sid) — a file named `2026_..​.jsonl`?? `_sessionIdFromPath` gives '..' → isSafePathSegment rejects → skipped as candidate. Test: a file named `<ts>_...jsonl`? Hmm '..' as basename sid — the file `202601_...jsonl` — the sid parse = '...' (three dots)? No: parts.last of '202601_..' minus .jsonl → '..'. File NAME '202601_...jsonl' = ts_ + '..' + '.jsonl'. OK so seed that filename directly via env.writeBinaryFile and assert it's skipped (no deletion of anything, no path outside root).
 Also symlinked usage dir: MemoryFileSystem has no symlinks — craft a FAKE fs wrapper that reports kind==symlink for the usage dir and assert _removeTree never removes it. Simpler: a fake FileSystem delegating to MemoryFileSystem but listing the usage dir as symlink kind... I can implement a small `_SymlinkReportingFs implements FileSystem` wrapper in the test that wraps MemoryFileSystem and overrides fileInfo for a specific path to return kind symlink. Then apply → usage dir survives. 

group 'REG-2 property':
 15. seeded random trees; invariants hold across shapes.

That's a lot but doable. Let me also plan the CLI-level tests after the core is green.

One more design check — `sweep()` ordering when multiple slugs: sort by lastUsed asc globally (E6). Good.

Test: current session exemption — currentSessionId passed.

Let me write the test file now.

And the mtime I set — setMtime to 2025-11-11 — but lastUsed shows 2026-10-21 19:50 = the E3 FLOOR at createdAt (header time 2026-10-21) since mtime (2025-11) < createdAt (2026-10-21). So lastUsed == createdAt == REAL NOW → the session is YOUNG (minAgeDays 0 → cutoff = fake now 2026-01-10 — wait, cutoff = _clockNow (2026-01-10) minus 0 = 2026-01-10. lastUsed (2026-10-21) is NOT before 2026-01-10 → too young → blocker!

The core problem: session creation stamps REAL now, but my fake clock is 2026-01-10 — in the PAST relative to real time. So every seeded session is "newer" than the fake clock → `lastUsed.isBefore(cutoff)` false → everything too young.

Fix: the fake clock must be in the FUTURE of real time (e.g. DateTime(2030)) OR seed ages relative to real time. Since `JsonlSessionRepo` uses its own `now` (injectable! `JsonlSessionRepo(..., now:)`) — I can pass `now: _clock` to the REPO too so headers carry fake-clock timestamps. That makes everything consistent. Also the mtime floor: createdAt = fake now; backdated mtimes (fake - 60d) < createdAt → E3 floor lifts lastUsed back to createdAt = fake now → YOUNG again! 

Ugh — the E3 floor interacts with test seeding: backdating mtime BEFORE creation makes lastUsed = createdAt (now) → young. In the earlier passing tests (AC4, usage) the blocker logic used minAgeDays 14 with ages... AC4 passed because it EXPECTED blockers.

Rethink test seeding: to get an OLD session (age > minAgeDays), the mtime must be older than now-14d BUT the E3 floor prevents mtime < createdAt. Since createdAt = fake now at seed time... I need createdAt to be BACKDATED too. JsonlSessionRepo.create uses `DateTime.now()` internally (create: `final createdAt = DateTime.now();`) — hmm, and JsonlSessionCreateOptions has no timestamp. The repo has a `now` field used for journal/trash stamps — is it used by create? Looking at the repo ctor: `now = now ?? DateTime.now` and `create` uses `DateTime.now()` directly (I saw `final createdAt = DateTime.now();` in create). So headers always carry REAL now.

Simplest robust approach: fake clock = REAL now + offset. `_clockNow = DateTime.now().add(...)` no — deterministic asserts on ages: use `clockNow = realNow` and ages as REAL durations: seed ages like 60 days → mtime = realNow - 60d; createdAt = realNow (header) → E3 floor lifts lastUsed to createdAt → young again. STILL broken.

So with the E3 floor, a session's lastUsed ≥ createdAt = REAL creation time. Any session I seed "now" can never appear older than minAgeDays unless minAgeDays ≈ 0! Because lastUsed is flored at creation (just now).

Hold on — that makes the E3 floor TOO aggressive for the minAgeDays semantics? Real-world: a session created 60 days ago has header timestamp 60d ago, mtime 1h ago → lastUsed = 1h ago → young. A session created 60d ago, last write 40d ago → mtime 40d ago > createdAt → lastUsed 40d. Fine. The floor only kicks when mtime < createdAt (restore). So for tests: seed a session, then BACKDATE... I can't backdate the header (it's written at create).

Option: rewrite the session file's header timestamp directly in tests (write the file manually with a backdated header). seedSession could: create via repo, then REWRITE line 1 with an edited timestamp (read file, replace timestamp string). That's honest (headers are just JSON) and gives full control. 

Simpler: `seedSession({DateTime? createdAt, DateTime? lastUsed})`: after create+appends, read the file text, replace the header timestamp ISO string with createdAt's ISO (if provided), write back, then setMtime(lastUsed). Since mtime ≥ createdAt ordering then holds by construction, no floor surprises.

Implementation: header timestamp format is ISO of creation (local? `timestamp.toIso8601String()`). I'll regex-replace the `"timestamp":"..."` field in the first line only. Careful: message records also carry timestamps — replace only the FIRST occurrence (the header line's). The header line starts `{"type":"session","version":3,"id":...,"timestamp":"...","cwd":...`.

Also minAgeDays comparisons then behave: createdAt backdated, mtime backdated ≥ createdAt → lastUsed = mtime.

Update seedSession in the test:
``
Future<String> seedSession({String? name, String cwd='/work', DateTime? createdAt, DateTime? lastUsed, int sizeBytes=0}) async {
 ... create/append ...
 final meta = await session.getMetadata();
 if (createdAt != null) {
   final raw = (await env.readTextFile(meta.path)).valueOrNull!;
   final patched = raw.replaceFirst(RegExp(r'"timestamp":"[^"]+"'), '"timestamp":"${createdAt.toIso8601String()}"');
   await env.writeFile(meta.path, patched);
 }

}
``

And the fake clock: keep deterministic `DateTime(2026,1,10,12)`; seed createdAt/lastUsed relative to it. Sessions: createdAt = daysAgo(90) default, lastUsed param. That kills the E3 floor surprises AND makes ages deterministic. REG-2: ages random, createdAt = daysAgo(ageDays+10), lastUsed = daysAgo(ageDays) (≥ createdAt).

``
final unitMin = usage.sessions.map((s) => s.bytes).reduce((a, b) => a < b ? a : b);
final cap = usage.totalBytes - unitMin * 2 + 1;
``
Hmm — units differ by name-record sizes; reduce min is safe: deleting the 2 oldest (each ≥ unitMin) frees ≥ 2*unitMin - 1... need total - 2u_min ≤ cap ⇔ 2u_min ≥ 2u_min - 1 ✓. And 1 deletion insufficient: total - u_i > cap ⇔ u_i < 2u_min - 1?? NO — if the oldest unit u1 ≥ 2*unitMin - 1, ONE deletion could suffice and middle stays. With equal-ish units (u ≈ u_min + small delta), 2u_min - 1 > u1 requires u1 < 2u_min - 1 — true when u_min < u1 + 1... u1 is the SMALLEST? oldest = first created; all identical shape (no names in this test) → u1 == u2 == u3 = u. cap = total - 2u + 1. One deletion: total - u vs cap = total - 2u + 1 → total - u > total - 2u + 1 ⇔ u > 1 ✓ → second deletion happens. After two: total - 2u ≤ total - 2u + 1 ✓ stop. Exact.

For 'keepNamed false': single session, cap = total - 20 → 1 deletion. Fix via unitMin: cap = total - 1 (any deletion brings it to ≤ total - u ≤ total - 1 given u ≥ 1) — cap = usage.totalBytes - 1 forces exactly the deletions needed... For a single candidate: cap = total - 1 → delete 1 → done. Use `total - 1`.

I need presence to change DURING apply. Hook: the sweper's `log` callback fires after a's deletion line — register b inside the log callback! `log: (line) { if (line.contains(a)) presence.register(b); }` — the apply loop awaits `_liveIds()` per action; log for a fires, register b (async fire-and-forget — race). Actually simpler: plan phase calls _liveIds once; apply calls before each action. So list() call #1 = plan…

The core problem: session creation stamps REAL now, but my fake clock is 2026-01-10 — in the PAST relative to real time. So every seeded session is "newer" than the fake clock → `lastUsed.isBefore(cutoff)` false → everything too young.

Fix: the fake clock must be in the FUTURE of real time (e.g. DateTime(2030)) OR seed ages relative to real time. Since `JsonlSessionRepo` uses its own `now` (injectable! `JsonlSessionRepo(..., now:)`) — I can pass `now: _clock` to the REPO too so headers carry fake-clock timestamps. That makes everything consistent. Also the mtime floor: createdAt = fake now; backdated mtimes (fake - 60d) < createdAt → E3 floor lifts lastUsed back to createdAt = fake now → YOUNG again! 

Ugh — the E3 floor interacts with test seeding: backdating mtime BEFORE creation makes lastUsed = createdAt (now) → young. In the earlier passing tests (AC4, usage) the blocker logic used minAgeDays 14 with ages... AC4 passed because it EXPECTED blockers.
