blocks.text:
## Tool-result spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and the
session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as `[spills]` notes at
boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` or `threshold: 0` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills):

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
```

Applies at next boot.

## Store & product links

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
p = 'prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md'
s = open(p).read()
old = "Applies at next boot.\n\n## Store & product links"
new = """Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Store & product links"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('ok')
EOF

{"content":"### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart

  SW --> LOG["fa.log [retention] lines + dim boot notice"]
  CLI2["fa session clean [--dry-run]"] --> SW
```

blocks.text:
## Tool-result spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and the
session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as `[spills]` notes at
boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` or `threshold: 0` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills):

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
```

Applies at next boot.

## Store & product links

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
p = 'prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md'
s = open(p).read()
old = "Applies at next boot.\n\n## Store & product links"
new = """Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Store & product links"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('ok')
EOF

{"content":"### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart
```
E2E: `HOME=<tmp> fa session clean --dry-run` with a `sessions.retention.maxTotalBytes` cap in `$HOME/.fah/config.yaml` — plan prints, nothing deletes; re-run without `--dry-run` to apply.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD

  AC --> BOOT["_retentionBootCheck() in _initializeSession"]
  BOOT --> SW["SessionRetentionSweeper.enforceAtBoot"]
  SW -->|"plan: oldest-first, exempt live/named/young"| DEL["delete whole units (re-check presence per unlink)"]
  SW --> LOG["fa.log [retention] lines + dim boot notice"]
  CLI2["fa session clean [--dry-run]"] --> SW
```

</details>

blocks.text:
## Tool-result spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and the
session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as `[spills]` notes at
boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` or `threshold: 0` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills):

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
```

Applies at next boot.

## Store & product links

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
p = 'prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md'
s = open(p).read()
old = "Applies at next boot.\n\n## Store & product links"
new = """Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Store & product links"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('ok')
EOF

Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. blocks.text:
## Tool-result spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and the
session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as `[spills]` notes at
boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` or `threshold: 0` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills):

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
```

Applies at next boot.

## Store & product links

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
p = 'prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md'
s = open(p).read()
old = "Applies at next boot.\n\n## Store & product links"
new = """Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Store & product links"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('ok')
EOF

blocks.text:
## Tool-result spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and the
session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as `[spills]` notes at
boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` or `threshold: 0` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills):

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
```

Applies at next boot.

## Store & product links

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
p = 'prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md'
s = open(p).read()
old = "Applies at next boot.\n\n## Store & product links"
new = """Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Store & product links"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('ok')
EOF

blocks.text:
## Tool-result spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and the
session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as `[spills]` notes at
boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` or `threshold: 0` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills):

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
```

Applies at next boot.

## Store & product links

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
p = 'prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md'
s = open(p).read()
old = "Applies at next boot.\n\n## Store & product links"
new = """Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Store & product links"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('ok')
EOF

blocks.text:
## Tool-result spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and the
session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as `[spills]` notes at
boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` or `threshold: 0` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills):

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
```

Applies at next boot.

## Store & product links

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
p = 'prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md'
s = open(p).read()
old = "Applies at next boot.\n\n## Store & product links"
new = """Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Store & product links"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('ok')
EOF

{"content":"### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)

blocks.text:
## Tool-result spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and the
session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as `[spills]` notes at
boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` or `threshold: 0` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills):

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
```

Applies at next boot.

## Store & product links

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
p = 'prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md'
s = open(p).read()
old = "Applies at next boot.\n\n## Store & product links"
new = """Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Store & product links"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('ok')
EOF

blocks.text:
## Tool-result spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and the
session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as `[spills]` notes at
boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` or `threshold: 0` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills):

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
```

Applies at next boot.

## Store & product links

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
p = 'prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md'
s = open(p).read()
old = "Applies at next boot.\n\n## Store & product links"
new = """Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Store & product links"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('ok')
EOF

Now wait for the full suite. While waiting, write outputs/response.md. Requirements: <20 lines, ### What changed / ### Key decisions / ### How to verify, optional mermaid in details, GFM, no filler.

{"content":"### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart
```
E2E: `HOME=<tmp> fa session clean --dry-run` with a `sessions.retention.maxTotalBytes` cap in `$HOME/.fah/config.yaml` — plan prints, nothing deletes; re-run without `--dry-run` to apply.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CFG["~/.fah/config.yaml sessions.retention"] --> CC["CliConfig (tolerant)"]
  CC --> AC["AgentCliConfig.sessionsRetention"]
  AC --> BOOT["_retentionBootCheck() in _initializeSession"]
  BOOT --> SW["SessionRetentionSweeper.enforceAtBoot"]
  SW -->|"plan: oldest-first, exempt live/named/young"| DEL["delete whole units (re-check presence per unlink)"]
  SW --> LOG["fa.log [retention] lines + dim boot notice"]
  CLI2["fa session clean [--dry-run]"] --> SW
```

</details>
","path":"outputs/response.md"}

blocks.text:
## Tool-result spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and the
session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as `[spills]` notes at
boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` or `threshold: 0` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills):

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
```

Applies at next boot.

## Store & product links

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
p = 'prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md'
s = open(p).read()
old = "Applies at next boot.\n\n## Store & product links"
new = """Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Store & product links"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('ok')
EOF

blocks.text:
## Tool-result spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and the
session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as `[spills]` notes at
boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` or `threshold: 0` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills):

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
```

Applies at next boot.

## Store & product links

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
p = 'prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md'
s = open(p).read()
old = "Applies at next boot.\n\n## Store & product links"
new = """Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Store & product links"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('ok')
EOF

blocks.text:
## Tool-result spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and the
session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as `[spills]` notes at
boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` or `threshold: 0` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills):

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
```

Applies at next boot.

## Store & product links

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
p = 'prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md'
s = open(p).read()
old = "Applies at next boot.\n\n## Store & product links"
new = """Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Store & product links"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('ok')
EOF

blocks.text:
## Tool-result spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and the
session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as `[spills]` notes at
boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` or `threshold: 0` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills):

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
```

Applies at next boot.

## Store & product links

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
p = 'prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md'
s = open(p).read()
old = "Applies at next boot.\n\n## Store & product links"
new = """Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Store & product links"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('ok')
EOF

blocks.text:
## Tool-result spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and the
session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as `[spills]` notes at
boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` or `threshold: 0` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills):

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
```

Applies at next boot.

## Store & product links

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
p = 'prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md'
s = open(p).read()
old = "Applies at next boot.\n\n## Store & product links"
new = """Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Store & product links"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('ok')
EOF

blocks.text:
## Tool-result spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and the
session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as `[spills]` notes at
boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` or `threshold: 0` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills):

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
```

Applies at next boot.

## Store & product links

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
p = 'prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md'
s = open(p).read()
old = "Applies at next boot.\n\n## Store & product links"
new = """Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Store & product links"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('ok')
EOF

blocks.text:
## Tool-result spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and the
session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as `[spills]` notes at
boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` or `threshold: 0` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills):

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
```

Applies at next boot.

## Store & product links

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
p = 'prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md'
s = open(p).read()
old = "Applies at next boot.\n\n## Store & product links"
new = """Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Store & product links"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('ok')
EOF

## Tool-result spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and the
session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as `[spills]` notes at
boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` or `threshold: 0` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills):

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
```

Applies at next boot.

## Store & product links

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
p = 'prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md'
s = open(p).read()
old = "Applies at next boot.\n\n## Store & product links"
new = """Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Store & product links"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('ok')
EOF

blocks.text:
## Tool-result spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and the
session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as `[spills]` notes at
boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` or `threshold: 0` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills):

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
```

Applies at next boot.

## Store & product links

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
p = 'prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md'
s = open(p).read()
old = "Applies at next boot.\n\n## Store & product links"
new = """Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Store & product links"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('ok')
EOF

You are Fa, a coding agent (also called fa). Never refer to yourself as pi, Claude, or any other assistant name. You help with software engineering tasks in the working directory /home/runner/work/flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness. Use the read, write, ls, and bash tools to inspect and modify files and run commands. Be concise.

## Session recall — never answer about the past from assumption

1. **Reference = search.** When the user references any past decision, rule, task, or artifact ("remember when…", "the rules we made", "that issue from last week"), call `session_search` BEFORE answering. Never answer about the past from assumption.
2. **Resume ritual.** After a compaction boundary is crossed or the session resumes, read the obligations ledger block (the `<system-notice>` titled "obligations ledger") first; it is the contract of what is still owed.
3. **Commit in the open.** Before promising a follow-up, check the ledger. When you arm a timer or watch (`schedule_message`), state the reason clearly in the message text — the engine writes a `pending-wait` ledger entry from it, and the fired timer re-enters a context that knows why it exists.
4. **Durable ≠ session.** Cross-session rules go to long-term memory immediately (`memory_add`); session-scoped obligations stay in the ledger. Never misuse either layer for the other.
5. **Dig idioms.** Markers are the TOC. `session_search` locates, `compact_expand` reads. `read $FAH_SESSION_FILE:<line>` is the zero-tool fallback.

## FinalizeGate — verify produced state before declaring done

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn made NO tool calls at all — no files written or edited, no commands run, nothing created or changed; a pure question answered from what you already know — there is nothing to verify. Skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise.

The contract does NOT apply to turns like:

- **"почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"** — a "why did you…" question. Just answer it directly: no checklist, no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what does the `read` selector `:N` do?"** — a "what does X do" question. Just explain it: no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what's the status?"** — a status/explanation answer about work already done. Report it plainly: no re-verification, no ledger.

Those turns produced no state; running the checklist ritual on them is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
2.5. **Grader parity** — your shell is not the verifier's: if the task ships a runnable verifier, test, or entry point the grader will call, run THAT command the way the grader will — neutral cwd (`cd /` — a different working directory, never the session cwd), fresh subprocess, clean env (no session-exported vars) — and compare stdout, stderr, and exit code against the earlier in-session run. Any divergence — different output, files created via relative paths now missing, locale/encoding-dependent output — is a `fail` item to fix before finalizing. The ledger row for the main artifact uses this invocation as its `command:`.
3. **Fix every unmet item** — a failed item is fixed and re-verified. Fix attempts are bounded: don't spiral on one dead end — switch approach.
4. **Final state is the deliverable** — never uninstall, stop, reset, or clean up what you produced while finalizing. Verification steps must be read-only or additive (a smoke probe, a curl, a diff) — never destructive. Cleanup happens only if the task explicitly requires it. ❌ Wrong: "verified, then reset to a clean state so the checker's commands run exactly as written" — the produced state no longer exists at grading, and that is a `fail`, not a clean handoff.

**Feasibility before commitment.** Before starting any step whose cost can dominate the remaining budget (from-source builds, large downloads, brute-force searches), estimate its duration and compare it against the time-left notices. If the estimate exceeds the budget, switch to a cheaper strategy that still satisfies the task (binary packages, targeted sub-builds, reduced scope the task allows) — or, when no satisfying strategy fits, the next-best partial — never gamble the whole window on a path you already know cannot finish.

**Work to the wall.** Your time-left notices report the remaining budget. While work remains, the next compliant action is another approach — not a final answer. Do not stop to wrap up: you are interrupted automatically when time expires, so no manual saving-up is needed. A final answer is written when the task is done or the deadline notice says so.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Archive extraction is complete** — after extracting a provided/downloaded archive into a target directory, diff the archive's full listing against the extracted tree (`unzip -l <archive>` / `tar -tf <archive>` vs `ls -R` of the target, or `find <target> -type f`); every entry — including root-level files with no extension and no obvious purpose (`file_id.diz`, `README`, `LICENSE`, version stamps) — must be present. A partial extraction is a `fail` item.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/.netrc`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed). The check runs against the state you leave behind: a file that existed mid-run but is deleted at finalization is a `fail` — final state is the deliverable (step 4).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it before the deadline, reported.

## Agent messaging

You have an inbox in the session-shared messaging fabric. Your address is `01a15fec-d8af-746b-a0e7-edfde9ee1e47/main`. Other Fa instances running in this project have their own inboxes — their orchestrators are reachable at `<theirSessionId>/main`, your subagents at their plain ids. Live instances also expose their session display name (`--session goal_builder`): `agent_directory` shows it next to the mailbox id, and `agent_message` accepts the name directly — `goal_builder` or `goal_builder/main` — so you rarely need the raw id. Use the `agent_directory` tool to list the live mailboxes (plus anything holding pending mail; pass `all: true` for long-dead ones and full mailbox ids — the default view truncates ids to save tokens) and `agent_message` to send. Each row also shows the last-activity time: `active 2m ago` means the watcher is live, `last active 3h ago (asleep)` means the process is gone. If you message an asleep target, the harness automatically launches a detached headless run of its session (`fa --session <name>`) to process the inbox; that run appends to the same session JSONL, so a later interactive start resumes the same conversation. Incoming mail is delivered to you automatically between turns (and wakes you when idle); reply with `agent_message` to the sender's address when a response is expected. Never guess mailbox addresses — read them from `agent_directory`.
When a hub is configured, `agent_directory` also lists hub peers beyond this project's file inboxes (embedded hosts, other machines) with their id and name — message them with `agent_message` the same way; the hub delivers even while a peer is offline (it drains when the peer reconnects).

Peers on OTHER machines are addressed `name@machine` (use a machine name you were told, or one from the peer itself): `agent_message to: "goal_builder@renderbox"` routes through the A2A gateway when this host's config has an `a2a.servers.renderbox` entry — delivery is synchronous there, so an error means the mail did NOT land (retry or tell the user). Without that config entry the send fails with the exact hint of what to add.

The owner's messages always arrive in YOUR inbox — subagents and children are your internal machinery, never the owner's address. Decide per message: answer directly when you know, or route it to the child doing that work with `task_send` and tell the owner you did (e.g. «передал fix503»); when the child's result lands, report it back. While children run you may go idle — the waiting row names them, and completions and new mail wake you.

content.text: `/outputs/` is git-ignored by design — post-processing reads it from disk. Final content check:

### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart
```
E2E: `HOME=<tmp> fa session clean --dry-run` with a `sessions.retention.maxTotalBytes` cap in `$HOME/.fah/config.yaml` — plan prints, nothing deletes; re-run without `--dry-run` to apply.

Note: `headless_log_file_test` and `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` (spawn-based E2Es that pick up the runner's real provider queue) fail on clean `origin/main` too — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CFG["~/.fah/config.yaml sessions.retention"] --> CC["CliConfig (tolerant)"]
  CC --> AC["AgentCliConfig.sessionsRetention"]
  AC --> BOOT["_retentionBootCheck() in _initializeSession"]
  BOOT --> SW["SessionRetentionSweeper.enforceAtBoot"]
  SW -->|"plan: oldest-first, exempt live/named/young"| DEL["delete whole units (re-check presence per unlink)"]
  SW --> LOG["fa.log [retention] lines + dim boot notice"]
  CLI2["fa session clean [--dry-run]"] --> SW
```

</details>

### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage…

blocks.text:
### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart
```
E2E: `HOME=<tmp> fa session clean --dry-run` with a `sessions.retention.maxTotalBytes` cap in `$HOME/.fah/config.yaml` — plan prints, nothing deletes; re-run without `--dry-run` to apply.

Note: `headless_log_file_test` and `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` (spawn-based E2Es that pick up the runner's real provider queue) fail on clean `origin/main` too — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CFG["~/.fah/config.yaml sessions.retention"] --> CC["CliConfig (tolerant)"]
  CC --> AC["AgentCliConfig.sessionsRetention"]
  AC --> BOOT["_retentionBootCheck() in _initializeSession"]
  BOOT --> SW["SessionRetentionSweeper.enforceAtBoot"]
  SW -->|"plan: oldest-first, exempt live/named/young"| DEL["delete whole units (re-check presence per unlink)"]
  SW --> LOG["fa.log [retention] lines + dim boot notice"]
  CLI2["fa session clean [--dry-run]"] --> SW
```

</details>
